fixes.explanation: Yes, baker. Acts 9:36 says Dorcas, a disciple in Joppa, was always occupied with works of kindness and charity. Always. Not once in a while. I'd love that on my own handle.
Eight years, friend. Acts 9:33 says Aeneas had been paralyzed and bedridden that long. I think that's a heavy stretch of time. Eight is the number to hold onto.

The saints are the ones Peter came to visit, friend (Acts 9:32). But when he speaks to Aeneas, he says, “Jesus Christ heals you!” The healing is credited to Jesus, not to the saints. They aren't the ones Peter names.
Yes, baker. Peter says, “Get up and put away your mat.” After eight years of lying down, that's quite a command. And the text says Aeneas got up immediately.
Lie still? That's the opposite of what Peter says, friend. He tells Aeneas, “Get up and put away your mat.” And the text says Aeneas got up immediately.

That's the one, baker. The text says all who lived in Lydda and Sharon saw him and turned to the Lord. The whole area saw Aeneas after he got up. It's hard to argue with what they saw: a man who'd been bedridden for eight years, and he got up.
That's it, baker. The disciples sent two men to urge Peter, “Come to us without delay.” They sent people to ask him in person. I think they wanted Peter there as fast as he could manage.
Letters would make sense, friend, but the text doesn't mention any. The widows showed Peter the tunics and other clothing that Dorcas had made. I think those clothes said plenty.
I think the quiet room fooled you, friend. The text says Peter, turning toward her body, said, “Tabitha, get up!” He speaks right to her, and the same verse says she opens her eyes.
Yes, baker. The text says she opened her eyes, and seeing Peter, she sat up. First the eyes open, then she sits up. Before that, Peter had knelt down and prayed.
No priests show up in this scene, friend. Peter called the saints and widows and presented Dorcas to them alive. The widows are the ones who had been standing around weeping.
No soldiers in this room, friend. The text says Peter called the saints and widows and presented her to them alive. The widows are the ones who had been showing Peter the clothing Dorcas made.
That's right, baker. The text says Peter stayed for several days in Joppa with a tanner named Simon. A tanner is someone who works with animal hides. Peter is the guest here, and Simon is the host.

Levi is a tax collector in the Gospel of Luke (Luke 5:27), friend. In this passage, the text says Peter stayed with a tanner named Simon. A tanner works with animal hides, not tax records. It's a fair mix-up, but the host is Simon.

Aquila is a tentmaker in a different story (Acts 18:2-3). Here the text says Peter stayed for several days in Joppa with a tanner named Simon. A tanner works with animal hides, friend. The host here is Simon, not Aquila.
